title: Local topological dimension for flat maps of constant relative dimension
statement: Let $f:X\to Y$ be a morphism of locally Noetherian schemes [pqf-def-locnoeth]. Assume $f$ is flat [def-weil-flat-morphism] and locally of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Let $d\in\mathbb N$, and suppose that for every $a\in X$, with $b=f(a)$ and scheme-theoretic fibre $X_b$ [def-pc-scheme-fibre], the local topological dimension at the point of $X_b$ corresponding to $a$ is $\dim_a(X_b)=d$ [def-kun-topological-dimension-at-point]. Then for every $x\in X$, with $y=f(x)$, one has $$\dim_x X=\dim_y Y+d.$$ All dimensions here are topological local dimensions, namely the minimum of the dimensions of open neighbourhoods, with $+\infty+d=+\infty$. No smoothness, surjectivity, separatedness, or global finite type hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Tag 0AFE, lemma-rel-dimension-dimension; relative dimension d written explicitly as dimension d at every point of every fibre

proof.text: Choose open neighbourhoods $U_0\ni x$ and $V_0\ni y$ with $\dim U_0=\dim_x X$ and $\dim V_0=\dim_y Y$, using the minimum in [def-kun-topological-dimension-at-point]. Since $Y$ is locally Noetherian and $f$ is locally of finite type, [pqf-lem-lft-fp-locnoeth] makes $f$ locally of finite presentation, so [lem-weil-pbc-flat-lfp-open] makes $f$ open. Put $U_1=U_0\cap f^{-1}(V_0)$, an open neighbourhood of $x$ contained in $U_0$. By [lem-weil-pbc-open-subspace-dimension-monotone] $\dim U_1\le\dim U_0=\dim_xX$, and the minimum in [def-kun-topological-dimension-at-point] gives $\dim U_1\ge\dim_xX$; hence $\dim U_1=\dim_xX$. Its image $V_1=f(U_1)$ is open because $f$ is open, contains $y$, and is contained in $V_0$; the same two inequalities give $\dim V_1=\dim_yY$. Replacing $X,Y,f$ by $U_1,V_1,h:=f|_{U_1}$, we may assume $h$ is surjective and $\dim X=\dim_xX$, $\dim Y=\dim_yY$.

source.place: Tag 0AFE, proof: shrink source and target to neighbourhoods of x and y, use openness, and shrink the target so the map is surjective

proof.text: The restricted schemes are open subschemes, so they remain locally Noetherian by [pqf-def-locnoeth]. Flatness restricts to $h$ by [def-weil-flat-morphism], since the local rings of the open subschemes $U_1$, $V_1$ are those of $X$, $Y$. For local finite type, let $a\in U_1$; by [lem-weil-pbc-lft-pointwise-criterion] there are affine opens $U\ni a$ of $X$ and $V$ of $Y$ with $f(U)\subseteq V$ and $\mathcal O_X(U)$ a finitely generated $\mathcal O_Y(V)$-algebra. Choose $g\in\mathcal O_Y(V)$ with $f(a)\in D(g)\subseteq V\cap V_1$ and then $s\in\mathcal O_X(U)$ with $a\in D(s)\subseteq U\cap U_1\cap f^{-1}(D(g))$; then $\mathcal O_X(U)_s$ is an $\mathcal O_Y(V)_g$-algebra generated by the generators of $\mathcal O_X(U)$ and $1/s$, so the same criterion, applied to the affine opens $D(s)\subseteq U_1$ and $D(g)\subseteq V_1$, makes $h$ locally of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. For $b\in Y$, [def-pc-scheme-fibre] identifies the underlying space of the fibre $X_b$ with $h^{-1}(b)$; therefore each fibre of $h$ is an open subspace of the corresponding original fibre. By [lem-weil-pbc-dimension-at-point-open-subspace], every point $a\in X_b$ still has $\dim_a(X_b)=d$. Thus the hypotheses on the fibres are preserved by the replacement.

source.place: Tag 0AFE, proof after shrinking: restricted morphism retains flatness and locally finite type, and the fibre dimension condition is unchanged on open neighbourhoods

proof.text: For every $b\in Y$, surjectivity makes $X_b$ nonempty. Every point of $X_b$ has local topological dimension $d$ by Step 2, so [lem-weil-pbc-dimension-supremum-local-dimensions] gives $\dim X_b=d$. (There are no empty fibres after the surjective replacement.)

source.place: Tag 0AFE proof invokes the supremum description of the dimension of a fibre; Tag 0B7I

proof.text: Fix $a\in X$, put $b=h(a)$, and write $R=\mathcal O_{Y,b}$ and $S=\mathcal O_{X,a}$. These are Noetherian local rings because $X$ and $Y$ are locally Noetherian. The stalk map $R\to S$ is flat by [def-weil-flat-morphism]. Let $\mathfrak Q$ be the prime of $S$ corresponding to $a$ and $\mathfrak p$ its contraction. The flat local dimension formula [lem-weil-pbc-flat-height-formula], together with the fibre-stalk identification [lem-sbc-scheme-fibre-stalk-quotient], gives $\dim\mathcal O_{X,a}=\dim\mathcal O_{Y,b}+\dim\mathcal O_{X_b,a}$. Now apply [lem-pc-scheme-dimension-local-rings] to $X$, $Y$, and every fibre $X_b$. Taking suprema over $a$ and grouping points by $b=h(a)$ yields $\dim X=\dim Y+d$, because Step 3 gives $\dim X_b=d$ for every $b$; the supremum manipulation is elementary and remains valid in the extended dimensions, with $+\infty+d=+\infty$.

source.place: Tag 0AFE, proof: apply Algebra Lemma 00ON pointwise and take the supremum over fibres, using Properties Lemma 04MU

proof.text: Finally, the open-subspace equality [lem-weil-pbc-dimension-at-point-open-subspace] gives $\dim_xX=\dim_x(U_1)=\dim U_1$ and $\dim_yY=\dim_y(V_1)=\dim V_1$. Substituting the equality from Step 4 proves $\dim_xX=\dim_yY+d$. The argument includes $d=0$, the identity morphism, empty schemes (the assertion is vacuous), and infinite base dimension; no smoothness, surjectivity, separatedness, or global finite-type assumption was introduced.
